what: The suite claimed the application writes the exit code nowhere but the process boundary, while two shipped commands write it from their own catch blocks and the declared blast radius named neither. Widened the scope to have both commands return their codes, and named the one remaining process read as a stated exception rather than leaving the claim unsatisfiable.

One scenario had no row in the scenario map and no edge in the control-flow graph, and the graph had no path for the extension where the command library rejects the invocation and records the code itself. Added the edge, the caller-side decision it exists for, and the missing map rows.

The export of the assembled report was guarded only against being stale or mis-wired, not against being reshaped on the way out. Added scenarios pinning the two properties a refactor would silently normalize.

Spec gate round 1 returned blocked at the governance pre-flight: the inline spec-producer declared the fixed-universal and procedural governances but none of the three backward-lens bars the gate grades against. Loaded all three and self-aligned before re-submitting.

Round 2 failed the deterministic suite check on two scenario-map rows that shared an edge and a path class, plus three judged fidelity defects: a row bound to a fabricated edge, a row naming an edge the graph does not contain, and two conventions for a non-flow row in one document. Settled one convention, rebound every structural row to it, and corrected the edge labels.

Round 3 found one control-flow edge with no scenario anywhere on the map: the path where the command library rejects the invocation, records the code itself, and the entry point returns zero. It is the branch the whole caller-side decision exists to protect, and it was covered only end-to-end through the executable, never at the entry point's own return. Added the scenario, mapped the edge, and wrote the test against the real command library rather than the stub, since a stub could only re-assert the design instead of testing it. Also retitled a scenario left stale when its body was widened.

The impl judge proved by mutation that the process boundary had no automated verification at all: inverting the condition that decides whether a returned code is applied left the whole suite green. Two frozen scenarios rested on manual end-to-end runs rather than on a check. Added a subprocess-level suite driving the executable and the generated launchers as real processes, covering both branches, and confirmed by re-running three mutations that each is now caught.
